Reference: Marler et al. (2022); Rajani et al. (2023); Bricker et al. (2024)
What is it: Pivot users opened the app almost twice as often as QuitGuide users, but abstinence did not differ significantly. QuitBot engaged well but its RCT was null
Why relevant: The selector's reward should combine proximal behaviour signals (cravings managed, plan kept), not just app opens

Reference: Bonell et al. (2015); notification-burden evidence (BMC Psychology, 2023)
What is it: Unintended effects: guilt after slips, notification annoyance, over-reliance on the app
Why relevant: Add dark-logic monitoring (annoyance, guilt check-ins) as negative rewards and stop rules (G7)

What is it: The stages-of-change model is criticised for arbitrary stage cut-offs and weak predictive value
Why relevant: Use HAPA with measured constructs, not TTM-style labels. Allow phase fall-back

Finding: COM-B is a framework, not a predictive model
What is it: Real-time COM-B "diagnosis" from sensors has no validation we could find
Why relevant: If COM-B is used, use it to design sub-models, not as a live classifier (correction to the early root sketches)

Finding: E-cigarettes are an effective cessation aid and the most-used one
Reference: Lindson et al. (2024) Cochrane living review; Jackson et al. (2025)
What is it: Nicotine e-cigarettes raise quit rates vs NRT (high certainty in the Cochrane review); used in ~40% of English quit attempts
Why relevant: Design decision needed: does the app support switching to e-cigs as a path? Policy differs by country, and Belgian stakeholders may have views

Finding: Explanations raise trust and acceptance of recommendations
What is it: Explanation goals: transparency, trust, persuasiveness, effectiveness, satisfaction
Why relevant: Our "why am I seeing this?" layer is testable in usability studies within our evaluation limits

Finding: A 2026 Dutch guideline on tobacco and nicotine addiction exists
What is it: Updated Dutch care guideline (also relevant for Flemish practitioners)
Why relevant: Align content (medication, counselling steps) with a guideline that our Flemish partners recognise

Reference: Crisis-handling evaluation (2025), arXiv:2509.24857; red-team study arXiv:2507.18905
What is it: General LLMs vary widely in detecting and responding to acute mental-health crises
Why relevant: Any free-text chatbot needs crisis detection and escalation (e.g. 1813 Zelfmoordlijn, Tabakstop, GP), tested before the user study

Finding: Ethics approval is needed for studies with smokers
Reference: UGent ethics committee procedures (to check); MDR Art. 62 ff. if device claims are made
What is it: Human-participant research needs ethics approval. A clinical investigation would apply only if we make medical claims
Why relevant: Lead time affects the study plan: start the application early (open question in PROGRESS)

Finding: Inclusivity is a stated user need
Reference: JMIR Formative Research (2023), e43603; Zhang et al. (2023)
What is it: Smokers from minority groups want culturally relevant content and examples
Why relevant: Building blocks need content variants. Recruit a diverse sample for the usability tests

Reference: Vlaanderen.be / Vlaams Instituut Gezond Leven (lists 7 quit-smoking apps); Tabakstop
What is it: Flemish public health bodies curate app lists
Why relevant: Distribution channel: being listed by Gezond Leven or Tabakstop counts more than store marketing (cf. trust, 05 M9)

What is it: Fewer smokers call the Flemish quitline
Why relevant: A digital entry point could feed users into the tabacologist pathway: a partner value proposition

Finding: Many cessation apps are abandoned by their makers
Reference: Review cited in QuitSure studies (2023; verify)
What is it: 88.5% of 104 apps had not been updated in over a year
Why relevant: Our framework must be maintainable by a partner after the course: modular content, documented claims

What is it: No smoking-specific JITAI meta-analysis; Sense2Stop results, full QuitBot paper and OKquit results not found
Why relevant: Be careful when claiming JITAI efficacy in reports; cite these as open
